newsitem.title: ITALY: No crime to bathe naked in public-Italian judge.
newsitem.headline: No crime to bathe naked in public-Italian judge.

text.p: An Italian judge ruled on Thursday that stripping naked to wash at a public fountain was not a crime -- as long as the fountain was in a secluded place.
Abderrahman Baid, a 29-year-old Moroccan, was cleared of affronting public decency on the grounds that his act did not constitute a crime.
His case was brought before summary court judge Antonella Duchini after police in the central city of Perugia came upon him and two compatriots washing at a fountain in a side street in August 1993.
The police report said Baid had his underpants down near his knees and was "bathing completely naked in a public place".
Duchini said she had based her ruling on common sense.

"It's one thing washing at a secluded fountain and another doing it at a fountain...right in the centre of Perugia," Duchini told reporters. "Basically what we were dealing with was three people of no fixed abode doing their best to have a wash".
